title: The Almost Prom
premise: Ivo Almeida just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built atop the ruins of a shuttered orphanage the school board razed in 1974. When his only friend, Priya Chandrasekaran, vanishes leaving behind a ring of keys that open doors that shouldn't exist beneath the school, Ivo is pulled into a buried scandal: children from the orphanage were quietly relocated and erased, and one of them never left. Guided by Priya's clues, the janitor who remembers too much, and a ghost girl named Wren who has waited fifty years to be found, Ivo uncovers the board's cover-up while the tunnels beneath the gym grow unstable. In the end, Ivo chooses exposure over safety—broadcasting the truth at prom itself—and Priya is found alive, Wren is finally named on the school's memorial wall, and Ivo learns that belonging isn't something you inherit; it's something you build.
about_author: Coral Hartwell writes young adult mysteries about quiet kids in loud towns, drawing on her years as a substitute teacher in small-town Ohio. She lives with two cats, an unreasonable number of houseplants, and a lifelong suspicion of school basements.

chapters.title: The New Kid Math
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Three weeks into Hollow Creek High, Ivo catalogs survival rules: sit near exits, answer nothing, be fine. Only Priya, his lab partner, breaks through with relentless friendliness. He almost enjoys it—then panics at how much he doesn't want to lose it. Emotional beat: guarded hope cracking open.

chapters.title: Cold Spots in Room 114
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya drags Ivo to investigate why Room 114 is always freezing and why the floor plan doesn't match the building's footprint. Ivo wants out; Priya smells a story for the school paper. Emotional beat: playful friction masking Priya's real obsession—her grandmother once lived nearby and 'lost' a sister.

chapters.title: The Keys Under the Bleachers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. After a fire drill, Priya texts him: found something huge, gym, 6pm. He arrives to an empty gym and a set of seven brass keys taped under the bleachers with her name scratched into them. No Priya. Emotional beat: dread arriving before understanding.

chapters.title: Missing, Presumed Truant
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The school calls Priya's disappearance a runaway case; her parents disagree; the administration closes ranks with unsettling speed. Ivo, the invisible kid, is suddenly the last person who saw her—and the vice principal watches him like a hawk. Emotional beat: isolation weaponized.

chapters.title: Seven Doors
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Testing the keys after hours, Ivo finds six fit nothing—until the seventh opens a maintenance door behind the boiler that opens onto stairs going down instead of up. Tunnels. Old wallpaper. A child's chalk drawing dated 1973. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: Mr. Okafor Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night janitor, Mr. Okafor, catches Ivo in the basement but instead of reporting him, goes pale at the keys. His own mother worked at St. Brigid's Home for Children before it burned—or didn't burn—in 1974. Emotional beat: an ally found in the least expected adult.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Deep in the tunnels, Ivo meets a girl in a faded uniform who knows his name. Wren doesn't age, can't leave, and insists Priya came looking for her sister's records—and went deeper, toward the sealed east wing. Emotional beat: terror softening into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (recovered journal entries). Intercut chapters reveal Priya's findings: the orphanage wasn't demolished legally; the land was sold cheap, records destroyed, forty-one children scattered and renamed. One child, Wren Almeida—no relation, Ivo checks twice—was never accounted for. Emotional beat: grief for strangers.

chapters.title: Detention Is a Doorway
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Framed for vandalism he didn't commit, Ivo gets detention—which puts him alone in the building at dusk, exactly where someone wants him. Footsteps follow. A warning note in his locker: STOP ASKING ABOUT 1974. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Vice Principal's Office
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo confronts Vice Principal Drayton, whose family name appears on the old deed. Drayton's denial is too practiced, too personal—his grandfather brokered the sale. But Drayton also seems afraid of something below, not just exposed above. Emotional beat: enemy revealed as fellow prisoner of history.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Ivo, Mr. Okafor, Priya's parents, and two classmates form a ragtag search party. Each brings a piece: a map fragment, a key's provenance, a memory. For the first time, Ivo stops calculating escape routes and starts planning rescue. Emotional beat: loneliness ending.

chapters.title: The East Wing Seal
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Six keys turn together in a rusted vault door—the seventh keyhole is empty. Behind it: the collapsed east wing, and evidence someone has been living there. Priya's jacket. Fresh footprints. And scratch marks counting days. Emotional beat: hope sharpened to a blade.

chapters.title: Prom Is Mandatory
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The school announces prom will proceed as scheduled—partly, Ivo realizes, because the gym sits directly over the tunnel junction, and the board needs the anniversary event as cover for a final 'renovation' pour that would seal everything forever. Deadline established. Emotional beat: ticking clock made literal.

chapters.title: Wren's Fifty Years
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren recounts the night of the 'fire': locked in during a punishment, left behind when the evacuation was quietly covered up. She shows Ivo how the tunnels shift, how time pools down here, and why she couldn't leave—but Priya might still be alive where she fell. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Seventh Key
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The missing seventh key turns up in Drayton's desk—he inherited it with the family guilt and never used it. Confronted with Wren herself, Drayton breaks, confessing what his grandfather did and handing over the key and the original deeds. Emotional beat: complicity met with mercy.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Prom night. While the gym fills above, Ivo, Okafor, and two friends descend with the seventh key as concrete trucks idle in the parking lot. The vault opens. Past the collapse, they find Priya—trapped, injured, alive, having survived on tunnel water and stubbornness. Emotional beat: reunion amid ruin.

chapters.title: The Long Way Up
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Carrying Priya through shifting tunnels as the renovation crew begins sealing entrances above, the group races Wren's knowledge of passages against the closing walls. Wren falters at the boundary she's never crossed. Ivo refuses to leave without her. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: Crossing Over
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the final threshold, Ivo takes Wren's hand and speaks her full name aloud—naming her back into the world. She crosses. Above, they emerge through the gym stage doors directly into prom, dust-covered, carrying proof. Emotional beat: triumph crashing into spectacle.

chapters.title: The Almost Prom
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Instead of fleeing, Ivo takes the microphone. With the deeds projected on the gym screen and Wren standing beside him, he tells everyone what happened in 1974. The room splits—some boo, some film, some weep—but the truth is loose and cannot be reburied. Emotional beat: courage over invisibility.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Documented
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Recovering in hospital, Priya publishes the full investigation. The state opens an inquiry; Drayton testifies; the renovation halts. Ivo visits daily, no longer calculating exits. Priya admits she chose him as a friend on day one because he looked like someone worth knowing. Emotional beat: bonds affirmed.

chapters.title: The Wall With Forty-Two Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Spring. The school dedicates a memorial wall bearing all forty-one children's names—and a forty-second added at Wren's request: Ivo Almeida, 'who came looking.' Not related by blood; claimed anyway. Ivo finally understands inheritance can be chosen. Emotional beat: belonging earned and given.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine. Actually.
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Graduation eve, Ivo walks the halls with Wren—now enrolled, now real, now annoyingly good at chemistry. The cold spot in Room 114 is just a broken radiator. He texts Priya one word—fine—and means it for the first time. Emotional beat: peace, hard-won and kept.
